title: Incremental S3 processing
prompt: You run the same Glue ETL job on a schedule and want to process only new or updated objects from the corresponding S3 source. What should you use?

choices.text: Change the database name in the Glue Data Catalog
choices.explanation: Changing metadata names does not track processed inputs.

choices.text: Use S3 versioning to control ETL inputs
choices.explanation: Version retention and the job's processing position are separate features.
They record input-processing state and enable incremental processing for supported sources.

learning.reason: Job bookmarks record input-processing state and enable incremental processing for supported sources.
learning.concept: Job bookmarks track the input side; deduplicating write results requires separate design.

category: データ取り込み・変換・運用
title: Athena read volume
prompt: You aggregate only some columns from daily logs in Athena. How can you reduce scanning by both date and column?

choices.text: Enable versioning for the S3 bucket
choices.explanation: Object history management does not narrow the range scanned by the query.
This enables partition pruning and column filtering.

choices.text: Compress a single CSV file with gzip
choices.explanation: Compression can help, but it does not provide date partitioning and column-level reads.

learning.reason: This approach enables partition pruning and column filtering.
learning.concept: Filter the partition key in the WHERE clause and specify only the required columns in SELECT.

category: データ取り込み・変換・運用
title: Incorporating updates
prompt: You want to apply updates to rows matching a key and add unregistered rows to an Iceberg table on S3 in a single Athena operation. What should you use?

choices.text: MERGE INTO with Athena engine version 3
choices.explanation: For a supported Iceberg table, it expresses matching rows along with updates and inserts.
A crawler discovers catalog metadata; it does not modify existing rows.

choices.text: Add all rows with INSERT INTO
choices.explanation: This does not update existing rows and may leave duplicates.

learning.reason: MERGE INTO expresses matching rows and updates or inserts for supported Iceberg tables.
learning.concept: Check the update and insert conditions and duplicate keys on the source side before executing MERGE.

category: データ取り込み・変換・運用
title: Bulk Loading from S3 to Redshift
prompt: You periodically load many S3 objects into Redshift. What method avoids inserting rows one at a time in the application?

choices.text: Insert each row individually from the client
choices.explanation: This makes it difficult to take advantage of parallelism and efficient loading.

choices.text: Only run a SELECT in Athena
choices.explanation: This retrieves query results but does not load data into Redshift.

choices.text: Use Redshift COPY with S3 as the input source
choices.explanation: This uses Redshift's parallel loading capability.

learning.reason: This uses Redshift's parallel loading capability.
learning.concept: Grant the IAM role used by COPY read access to the input data, and verify the file format and error logging settings.

category: データ取り込み・変換・運用
title: Table-Level Permissions
prompt: In the same data lake, you need to manage which catalog tables and columns each analyst is allowed to access. What is appropriate?

choices.explanation: Together with supported engines, these permissions can manage access at the table and column levels.

choices.text: Use only an S3 bucket policy
choices.explanation: It can control file access, but it does not evaluate catalog permissions at the column level.
Key version management is separate from column-level access management.

learning.reason: Together with supported engines, these permissions can manage access at the table and column levels.
learning.concept: In addition to logical data lake permissions, verify that users do not unintentionally retain direct S3 access.

category: データ取り込み・変換・運用
title: A Replayable Stream
prompt: For a new aggregation process, you want to reread the most recent 7 days of records still retained in Kinesis. What should you configure beforehand?

choices.explanation: This affects consumer read throughput but does not change the retention period.

choices.text: Only increase the number of shards
choices.explanation: This affects processing capacity, but expired records are not retained.

choices.text: Set the stream retention period to at least 7 days
choices.explanation: A new consumer can reread records from sequence positions that remain within the retention period.

learning.reason: A new consumer can reread records from sequence positions that remain within the retention period.
learning.concept: The retention period determines how far back records can be reread; the consumer's processing position is managed separately.
